title: Global menu should still show KWin-provided window management features when a window that doesn't support Global Menu is open
line: The Global Menu now shows a Window menu with minimize, maximize, fullscreen, move, resize, keep above/below, move to desktop and close for apps that have no menu of their own.
explanation: The Global Menu only showed menus that the active window exports over D-Bus, so for apps without a menu bar (System Settings, xterm and most Kirigami or non-KDE apps) it stayed empty, including apps that export an empty menu. Now, when the active window has no menu or an empty one, the applet builds a Window menu from the task manager model with the window actions KWin's own window menu offers (Minimize, Maximize, Fullscreen, Move, Resize, Keep Above/Below Others, Move to Desktop when there is more than one desktop, Close). Enabled and checked states follow the window, actions go through the same TasksModel requests the task manager uses, and apps with a real menu are unchanged.

commits.message:
applets/appmenu: show a Window menu for windows without a menu

The Global Menu stayed empty for windows that don't export a menu, or
export an empty one. It now shows a Window menu for them with the same
window management actions KWin's own window menu offers.

BUG: 481628

media.caption: Master: System Settings is active and the Global Menu in the top panel is empty.
With the fix: the Global Menu shows a Window menu for System Settings; Maximize is checked because the window is maximized.
Move to Desktop lists All Desktops, each desktop (the current one checked) and New Desktop; picking Desktop 2 moved the window there.
After choosing Keep Above Others, the menu shows it checked.
